The hypervisibilization of girls of color in Disney’s performative wokeness: a cultural analysis of Disney corporate communication

Diana Leon-Boys; Kailin Regutti

Disney has walked a tightrope in its public relationship to “wokeness,” amplifying and scaling back commitments to diversity and inclusion, most recently through the removal of its “Reimagine Tomorrow” program. This essay examines this tension across Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) reports produced from 2019–2022. Chaperoning freedom: histopoetics, #hashtag activism, and the ongoing struggle for liberation

Anjuliet G. Woodruffe

This paper explores the intersections of historical and contemporary struggles for Black freedom in the United States through the construct of chaperoning freedom. By demonstrating how Black freedoms have been historically disciplined, the author uses Black feminist autoethnography, and histopoetics, to navigate the tension between past injustices and present-day political policies. Performing patriarchy through play: entertainment-symbolic misogyny and the queer reproduction of gender on Douyin

Shiyi Liao

This article examines how misogynistic logics are reproduced through gay men’s digital practices on Douyin. Drawing on twenty-one semi-structured interviews and thematic analysis, it analyzes the consumption of vulgarized female influencers and feminized performances among gay men. Tea as a communicative medium: materiality and the everyday life in Shandong Province

This article analyzes the transformative trajectory of tea practice in an urban village in China, examining how evolving tea drinking and the tearoom foster communication in a relocated community undergoing urbanization.
